questions.prompt: How does `Script-Migration` (`dotnet ef migrations script`) differ from `Update-Database`?
options: It creates a new migration file from model changes
It generates the SQL for your migrations instead of applying them to the database
It removes the last migration
It scaffolds entity classes from an existing database
questions.explanation: `Script-Migration` converts your migrations into the SQL EF Core would run and writes a script, instead of directly updating the database like `Update-Database` does.

questions.prompt: Why generate the production script with `--idempotent`?
options: It makes the script run faster by skipping indexes
It removes `DROP COLUMN` statements so no data is lost
It applies only the migrations not yet applied, so it is safe to run on a database in any migration state
It runs every migration again from the start to rebuild the schema
questions.explanation: An idempotent script can be run multiple times without errors: it checks which migrations already exist and applies only the missing ones, which suits production where the exact DB version may vary.

questions.prompt: Put the production deployment flow in order.
questions.explanation: The database is backed up and migrated (and checked) before the new API version is deployed, followed by a smoke test; database changes go out before the API.

questions.prompt: Which reason does the lesson give for **not** calling `db.Database.Migrate()` at application startup in production?
options: Multiple app instances may run the migrations at the same time
`Migrate()` only works with SQLite
`Migrate()` deletes the `__EFMigrationsHistory` table
It can only apply the first migration
questions.explanation: The reasons listed are: multiple instances may run migrations simultaneously, slower startup, elevated DB permissions are needed, and it is harder to audit and control.

options: `-OutputDir` and `-Context`
`-Tables` and `-Schemas`
`-DataAnnotations` and `-Force`
The connection string and the database provider
questions.explanation: `-Connection` (the connection string of the database to reverse-engineer) and `-Provider` (such as `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer`) are required; the rest are optional.

questions.prompt: You scaffolded models from an existing database and then ran `add-migration`. Why does `update-database` fail for that first migration?
options: Scaffolded models can never be used with migrations
The tables already exist in the database
`add-migration` doesn't work on scaffolded models
The scaffolded context has no `OnModelCreating` method
questions.explanation: The first migration tries to create tables that already exist. The fix is to script the migration and run only the `CREATE TABLE [__EFMigrationsHistory]` and `INSERT INTO [__EFMigrationsHistory]` parts against the database.
